# Describe numeric data (stats.describe)

## categories

[
  "statistics",
  "math"
]

## demonstrations

[
  {
    "expected_output": {
      "count": 4,
      "mean": 2.5,
      "median": 2.5,
      "quantiles": {
        "q1": 1.75,
        "q2": 2.5,
        "q3": 3.25
      },
      "stdev": 1.118033988749895,
      "variance": 1.25
    },
    "id": "four-values",
    "input": {
      "values": [
        4,
        1,
        3,
        2
      ]
    },
    "title": "Four unsorted observations"
  },
  {
    "expected_output": {
      "count": 1,
      "mean": 7,
      "median": 7,
      "quantiles": {
        "q1": 7,
        "q2": 7,
        "q3": 7
      },
      "stdev": 0,
      "variance": 0
    },
    "id": "singleton",
    "input": {
      "values": [
        7
      ]
    },
    "title": "A single observation"
  }
]

## description

Summarize a bounded list of finite JSON numbers. Variance and standard deviation describe the supplied population (divisor n, not sample divisor n-1). Quartiles q1/q2/q3 are the 25th/50th/75th percentiles, using inclusive endpoint linear interpolation (Python statistics.quantiles inclusive). Singleton quartiles all equal the sole value. Returns rounded binary floating-point values, not exact symbolic results. No files are read or written.

    "recovery": "Supply a bounded nonempty numeric list; do not encode expressions or missing values.",
    "symptom": "Input validation or capability error."
  }
]

## limitations

[
  "1 to 10000 finite numbers, each between -1e12 and 1e12 inclusive. Booleans and numeric strings are rejected.",
  "Population statistics summarize only the supplied values; no confidence interval, missing-value inference or causal conclusion is computed.",
  "Binary floating-point rounding, including underflow for extremely small variances, applies. Quartiles use the explicitly documented inclusive convention."
]

## name

Describe numeric data
